title: Reranker shard failure isolation and smart-retry/fallback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket implements per-shard failure isolation for the reranking fleet, introduces a multi-tiered smart-retry policy, and wires a regional-aware fallback orchestration layer. Goals: reduce end-to-end P99 latency regressions under partial shard failure, avoid cascading retries that amplify outages, and provide deterministic fallback behavior to cheaper embedding-only or cached partial results when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: P99 tail latency for rerank requests remains within 1.5x baseline during a simulated 15% shard failure across region A
Successful circuit-open events should prevent more than 5% of downstream queued requests from being retried to unhealthy shards during the test window
Fallback path returns ranked candidates from cache or nearest healthy region within configured timeout and has telemetry tags to indicate degradation reason
No more than 10% increase in successful rerank errors surface to customers; most failures should be converted to graceful fallback responses
technical_notes: Introduce per-shard health score computed from recent latency, error-rate, and queue-depth. Health score is broadcast to local route table every 5s.

Circuit breaker policy: error-rate threshold (sliding window 60s), consecutive timeout threshold, and exponential backoff open-window. Circuit state stored in local in-memory store and replicated via Raft overlay for cross-process visibility.

Smart-retry engine: fast failover (<50ms) to alternate local shard or sibling region when health score below threshold; limited number of retries (configurable, default 1) and use jittered backoff to avoid sync retries.
Fallback orchestration: preference order = local healthy shard -> regional peer -> cache-> embeddings-only proxy. Each tier has its own SLO budget and cost multiplier.
Timeout inheritance: client-specified deadline propagated; per-hop time allocation uses proportional split with minimum leaf timeout of 50ms to allow cached returns.
Telemetry: add rerank.failure_mode tag (SHARD_UNHEALTHY, CIRCUIT_OPEN, TIMEOUT, CACHE_HIT_FALLBACK) and detailed timing spans for routing, queueing, execution, and retry delays.
Compatibility: API surface unchanged. Internal routing config gated behind runtime flag 'rerank.smart_fallback_v1' for canary rollout.
progress_updates: 2025-03-06: Spike complete — proof-of-concept health scoring implemented on a single rerank node. Verified health transitions on synthetic elevated latency.
2025-03-08: Implemented basic circuit-breaker states and unit tests. Noted edge case: transient GC pauses caused spurious opens — added hysteresis to health score.

2025-03-10: Integrated smart-retry engine with local route table. Initial integration tests show 30% fewer tail failures but increased cross-region calls in worst-case. Need policy to cap cross-region failovers.
2025-03-11: Added telemetry tags and dashboard panel prototype (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/2187). Live canary started in us-west-2 on 2% of traffic.
2025-03-12: Canary observed expected fallback behavior during induced shard drain; awaiting perf run with 15% induced shard failures.
Next: run large-scale chaos experiment and iterate on cross-region cap strategy.
decisions: Use local in-memory circuit state with lightweight replication rather than centralized store to reduce lookup latency.
Default retry count set to 1 to minimize amplification; make it configurable per-traffic-class.
Prefer regional peer over global region to balance latency/cost tradeoffs; cross-region only when regional budget is exhausted.
Expose feature behind runtime flag for gradual rollout and quick rollback on regression.
review_feedback: PM (Elena Morales): Ensure SLA impact is communicated to customers when fallback becomes active and add telemetry to Console to expose graceful-degradation events.
Design (Ravi Gupta): Add UX signal in Console per-route showing percent of requests served by fallback tiers for last 24h.
SRE (Jing Zhao): Circuit open replication must survive node restarts; prefer write-ahead log and fast recovery. Also request capacity blast test before enabling cross-region failover.
Security: verify that cache fallback does not leak tenant-specific restricted content — implement tenant-aware cache keys (action assigned to ENG-75412).
